questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was mainly interested in English-speaking destinations. I also saw exchange as an opportunity to visit a faraway place. Another thing I prioritised was a university that would be somewhat close to the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. The University of Melbourne makes it very clear that you can go to Stop 1 if you need any help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction week where we got a lot of information and were able to seek help if we needed it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The introduction week was one week before the official start of uni so keep this in mind when booking flight tickets. You don't want to miss the introduction week both for social and practical reasons.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We found the rent to be quite expensive in Melbourne and it was difficult to find housing. I would recommend using the Facebook group Fairy Floss to search for housing. If you want to live in student accommodation I would recommend looking for the smaller businesses as they are cheaper than for example Scape and UniLodge.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are many cool places to live in Melbourne, so living off campus is super nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You choose the subjects you want. Then you can edit your schedule so it suits you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always contact stop 1.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up being pretty satisfied with the subjects I took. However, the process was a bit stressful in the beginning. It is easy to choose the subjects you want to take and to customize a schedule that suits you. But when changing some of my subjects during the first week (though it is nice that you have the opportunity to do so) I found that a lot of the subjects were full or clashed with my other subjects. You may have to compromise.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice is to check out your chosen subjects pretty thoroughly just so you have better odds at avoiding changing subjects.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one first-year subject, two second-year subjects and one third-year subject.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found it pretty similar to ucph. The teaching style varied from subject to subject just like it does at ucph. I had lectures (three out of four were unfortunately online pre-recorded) and tutorials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Performance, Potential and Development
- Diplomat, Soldier, Spy: The Deep State
- Internet Communication
- Marketing Communications

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Diplomat, Soldier, Spy: The Deep State if you are interested in surveillance, technology and the relationship between state and citizen. It is an anthropology course so it may be a bit different compared to the courses you have been through in Communication and IT.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In most student accommodation stuff for the kitchen (plates, knives, cups, pots and pans etc.) is not included.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was definitely more expensive than expected. Eating out and grocery shopping was also more expensive than expected. Eating out is probably the same as in Denmark. Groceries may even be a bit more expensive compared to Denmark. Alcohol is also super expensive. Except for the wine which is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many sports opportunities and also a lot of different cultural clubs available.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost any sports. Language specific clubs, book clubs, wine clubs, environment clubs etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I was a part of the athletics club where we ran each Monday and Wednesday. You weren't expected to come each time, you could join as you pleased. They have different teams for different levels. I joined the development team which was both for beginners and those who join competitions. 
I was also a part of the wine club. I enjoyed it although there was only 1 event during the semester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend going travelling in the mid-semester break or whenever you feel like you have time. If you are travelling around Australia I would recommend considering the weather and when it is best to visit the different places. Some places up north go into rain season and stinger season.
Also highly recommend visiting Byron Bay when it is "beach weather".

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. There were many cultural differences but non of them were of any major importance.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Australians are very welcoming and friendly people. Not like danish people they don't mind speaking to strangers. Through my job working in an ice cream shop, I also met locals. I highly recommend getting a part-time job.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I hated that cafés closed at around 2 pm haha. But nothing challenging I would say.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated that Australians are very open and approachable. I loved their day drinking and barbecue meet-ups.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. There is plenty to do and see in and around Melbourne. 
2. Don't forget to bring warm clothes. My semester in Melbourne was colder than usual. But in general, the temperatures can go from 23 degrees one day to 12 degrees the next day.
3.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed working beside my studies. It is super easy to get a job in Australia at the moment. I worked in an ice cream shop. The pay is good, you get to meet a lot of new people and you feel more like a part of the city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have met a lot of other exchange students from Denmark and other countries who I have become great friends with.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was probably finding housing. It wasn't that I was afraid that I would end up on the streets. It was just difficult finding something that wasn't too expensive or too far away.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
